extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry; readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt treating codimension and dimension phenomena: Krull's Principal Ideal and Height Theorems, Algebraic Hartogs, fiber-dimension behavior, and related exercises and applications (lines on hypersurfaces, UFD criterion, semicontinuity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Most degree d>3 surfaces in P^3 contain no lines (Exercise 11.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: ENLIGHTENING STRENUOUS EXERCISE: For any d > 3, show that most degree d surfaces in P^3 over an algebraically closed field k contain no lines. 'Most' means all closed points of a Zariski-open subset of the parameter space for degree d homogeneous polynomials in 4 variables, up to scalars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Construct an incidence correspondence X = {(ℓ,H) : [ℓ] ∈ G(1,3), [H] ∈ P^{(d+3 choose 3)-1}, ℓ ⊂ H}, view X as a P^{(d+3 choose 3)-1-(d+1)}-bundle over G(1,3) (use cover by A^4), compute dim X = (d+3 choose 3)-1-(d+1)+4, then show the image of projection X*→P^{(d+3 choose 3)-1} lies in a proper closed subset. Remark: argument generalizes: if d > 2n-3, most degree d hypersurfaces in P^n have no lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change independence of dimension for finite type schemes (Remark on Exercise 11.2.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is described by equations with Q-coefficients, the dimension of X doesn’t depend on whether we consider it as a Q-scheme or as a C-scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Exercise 11.2.J (conceptually useful); finite-type hypotheses on X are important — arbitrary schemes under arbitrary extensions need not preserve purity of dimension (see later counterexamples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem (geometric version, 11.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a locally Noetherian scheme, and f is a function. The irreducible components of V(f) are codimension 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric translation of the algebraic version; used most often for varieties. See algebraic version 11.3.3 for the ring-theoretic statement and proof references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem (algebraic version, 11.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a Noetherian ring, and f ∈ A. Then every prime p minimal among those containing f has codimension at most 1. If furthermore f is not a zero-divisor, then every such prime p has codimension precisely 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to deduce that locally principal closed subschemes have components of codimension 0 or 1, and that effective Cartier divisors have pure codimension 1. Applicable to varieties and Noetherian localizations; see exercises for concrete applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypersurfaces meet positive-dimensional projective subsets (Exercise 11.3.C(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If X ⊂ P^n_k is a closed subset of dimension at least 1 and H is a nonempty hypersurface in P^n_k, then H meets X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider affine cones; apply Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem to the cone over X and the cone over H. This exercise underlies many intersection existence results in projective space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear spaces meet projective varieties of complementary dimension (Exercise 11.3.C(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If X ⊂ P^n_k is a closed subset of dimension r, then any codimension r linear space meets X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine the argument from (a); useful for intuitive dimension-counting intersection facts (generalized in Exercise 11.3.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of hypersurfaces avoiding components (Exercise 11.3.C(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X of dimension r in P^n_k, there exists an intersection of r+1 nonempty hypersurfaces missing X; if k is infinite one can find a codimension r+1 linear subspace missing X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct hypersurfaces of sufficiently high degree not vanishing on generic points; proceed by induction on number of generic points and multiply polynomials appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite intersection giving finite points for infinite base field (Exercise 11.3.C(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is infinite and X ⊂ P^n_k has dimension r, there is an intersection of r hyperplanes meeting X in a finite number of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prepares for defining degree; for algebraically closed k, 'most' choices give reduced intersections whose size equals degree (later chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound on codimension of intersections in A^n (Exercise 11.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are equidimensional closed subvarieties of codimensions m and n in A^d_k, then every component of X∩Y has codimension at most m + n in A^d_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify intersection with intersection of X×Y with diagonal ∆ in A^d×A^d where ∆ is a regular embedding of codimension d, and apply Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem; use Exercise 11.2.E as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertibility criterion from absence in low-codimension primes (Exercise 11.3.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ A (Noetherian ring) is contained in no codimension 0 or 1 prime ideals, then f is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that a nowhere-vanishing function on Spec A is invertible (cf. Exercise 4.3.G(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: UFD characterization via codimension-1 primes (Proposition 11.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a Noetherian integral domain. Then A is a unique factorization domain iff all codimension 1 prime ideals are principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction is immediate; conversely principal codimension-1 primes give prime elements, irreducible=prime, and standard arguments yield existence and uniqueness of factorizations. See relation to Lemma 11.1.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull's Height Theorem (11.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X = Spec A where A is Noetherian, and Z is an irreducible component of V(r1, ..., r_ℓ) with r1,...,r_ℓ ∈ A. Then codimension of Z is at most ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization of the Principal Ideal Theorem. See §11.5 for proof. Use to deduce bounds on how many equations cut out a given codimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: System of parameters (Definition 11.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian local ring (A,m) of dimension d, there exist g1,...,gd ∈ m such that V(g1,...,gd) = {[m]}; such elements are called a system of parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric translation: a d-dimensional germ can be cut out set-theoretically by d equations, and one always needs at least d equations. Exercise 11.3.I provides algebraic existence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathologies of codimension (11.3.9 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: A = k[x](x)[t] (polynomials in t with coefficients rational functions in x having no x in denominator). Then (xt−1) is a maximal ideal of codimension 1 but corresponds to a dimension-0 component, showing codimension can behave oddly in some Noetherian rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition: Spec k[x](x) is a 'germ' of A^1 near origin; V(xt−1) avoids V(x) and so has no specialization there. This illustrates why care is needed with codimension in non-catenary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic Hartogs's Lemma (11.3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an integrally closed Noetherian integral domain, then A = ⋂_{p codimension 1} A_p inside K(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: a rational function on a Noetherian normal scheme with no poles (i.e., lies in all codimension-1 localizations) is actually regular. Use to connect line bundles and divisors; alternative proofs use Serre's criterion for normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for existence of lines through a point on hypersurface (Exercise 11.3.J(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a homogeneous polynomial f = f_d(x1,...,xn) + x0 f_{d-1} + ... + x0^{d-1} f_1 cutting out a hypersurface X ⊂ P^n containing p=[1:0:...:0], show there's a line through p contained in X iff f_1 = f_2 = ... = f_d = 0 have a common zero in P^{n-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: given a common zero [a1:...:an] in P^{n-1}, show line joining p to [0:a1:...:an] lies in X. Part (b),(c) use Exercise 11.3.C to deduce generic nonexistence of such lines for appropriate degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension inequality for morphisms (Key Exercise 11.4.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X→Y is a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, and p∈X, q∈Y with q = π(p). Then codim_X p ≤ codim_Y q + codim_{π^{-1}(q)} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take a system of parameters for q in Y and for p in the fiber π^{-1}(q) and combine to get elements cutting out p in Spec O_{X,p}; use Exercise 11.3.I. This formalizes that fiber dimensions cannot drop unexpectedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic fiber dimension theorem (Theorem 11.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite-type morphism π: X→Y of irreducible k-varieties with dim X = m and dim Y = n, there exists a nonempty open U ⊂ Y such that for all q ∈ U the fiber π^{-1}(q) has pure dimension m−n (or is empty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses generic-fiber arguments, embedding into A^{m−n} over the function field K(B), Noether normalization, and 'spreading out' by inverting finitely many denominators (distinguished open D(f)). Use Exercise 11.4.B to complete dimension estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension (Theorem 11.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For a finite-type morphism π: X→Y of k-schemes, the function p↦dimension of the fiber of π at p (i.e., dimension of largest component of π^{-1}(π(p)) containing p) is upper semicontinuous on X. (b) If π is closed (e.g., proper), then q↦dimension of the fiber over q is upper semicontinuous on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on dim Y, using Theorem 11.4.1 to find open set where relative dimension is constant and applying Exercise 11.4.A. Counterexamples exist to (b) if closedness hypothesis is dropped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generically finite implies finite above dense open (Proposition 11.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X→Y is a generically finite morphism of irreducible k-varieties of the same (pure) dimension n, then there is a dense open V ⊂ Y above which π is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to affine case and follow Noether-normalization-style arguments from Theorem 11.4.1; cover X by finitely many affine opens where π is finite and show the union of their images contains a dense open subset of Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity phenomena (Aside 11.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of commonly occurring semicontinuous functions in algebraic geometry: (i) fiber dimension (upper semicontinuous), (ii) rank of matrix of functions (lower semicontinuous), (iii) rank of a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf (upper), (iv) degree of a finite morphism (upper), (v) dimension of tangent space at closed points (upper), (vi) rank of cohomology groups of coherent sheaves in proper flat families (upper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an eye for semicontinuity: most geometric invariants exhibit upper semicontinuity, with some notable lower-semicontinuous exceptions (e.g., matrix rank).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of fiber-dimension results beyond varieties (11.4.5–11.4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments for Theorem 11.4.1 and Theorem 11.4.2 extend beyond varieties to locally Noetherian schemes and, with care, to finite-type morphisms over Spec of finitely-generated Z-algebras; excellent rings (e.g., Z and its finitely-generated algebras) allow 'spreading out' arguments to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key tools: codimension = difference of dimensions in catenary contexts (Theorem 11.2.9), Noether normalization over the function field, and localization/inverting finitely many denominators to obtain distinguished opens where the generic statements hold.
